newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Morning Update.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Morning Update.

text.p: HOWARD TO FACE OPPOSITION PRESSURE
Prime Minister, John Howard, has dismissed Opposition claims of sleaze in his Government.
The Opposition is expected to pressure Mr Howard today on when he first knew of the Federal Police investigation of a complaint concerning Parliamentary Secretary, Bob Woods.
Mr Howard has revealed he was informed of the complaint late last year by the Attorney-General.
His office says he didn't recall that when he told a television interviewer on Tuesday Senator Woods had informed him ten days before allegations were being investigated.
The office denies that statement was misleading, saying Mr Howard wasn't saying and wasn't asked when he first knew.
Opposition leader, Kim Beazley, says it's most unusal for a Prime Minister to forget a briefing on a police investigation into one of his Parliamentary Secretaries.
SENATE MAY BLOCK POSTAL VOTE FOR CONVENTION DELEGATES
Mounting opposition to the Federal Government's plan for a voluntary postal vote for delegates to this year's Constitutional Convention, may see the process blocked by the Senate.
The Government has put forward the option of a voluntary postal vote as one way of meeting its promise to have half the convention's delegates elected.
Federal Liberal MP Joe Hockey has questioned the effectiveness of postal ballots.
The Opposition leader Kim Beazley says the process would be akin to a logies-style popularity contest.
And the Democrats say a voluntary ballot would compromise the convention's authority because it would be elected without a wide mandate.
NEW LEVEE BANKS PROTECT CUNAMULLA

New levee banks are holding up in the south western Queensland town of Cunamulla, downstream of Charleville. The Warrego river is expected to reach ten metres this morning - and the new levy banks are 11 metres high.

The river reached 10.25 meters at the peak of the 1990 floods. The shire's chief executive officer, Sue Beresford, says she's expecting the flood waters which peaked in Charleville on Tuesday to reach Cunnamulla possibly tomorrow.
She says council workers laboured all night finishing off new levee banks which had been due for completion by the end of the financial year.
ABA PROMOTES DIGITAL TELEVISION

The Australian Broadcasting Authority says digital television will enable eixsting commercial networks to choose between broadcasting one high quality signal, or several lesser quality programmes at once.
ABA Chairman Peter Webb told a television technology conference in Sydney, commercial networks will pay more than A$200 million early next century to convert to digital television.
The new channels will be broadcast within the frequency spectrum now used to broadcast just one channel.
Mr Webb says networks will be to go from high definition mode, for major events such as a major sporting spectacular or a blockbuster movie, to a multi-channel mode.
COWLEY TO HEAD SUPER LEAGUE BOARD
News Limited's executive chairman Ken Cowley is to head the board of Superleague.
Eleven members will sit on the board, six of which are News Limited nominees and five nominees of Superleague clubs.
So far News Limited has nominated five men. John Brass, Ian Frykberg, John Ribot, Sir Roger Douglas and Ken Cowley.
The clubs have so far nominated four men, Roger Cowan, Anthony Ayres, Stephen Edwards and Peter Gow.
The two remaining board seats are expected to be filled soon.
JAPANESE ARRIVALS DOWN
The number of Japanese visitors to Australia in November was nine thousand down on November 1995.
In a continuing downward trend in Australia's most significant inbound tourist market, 55-thousand Japanese holidaymakers arrived in November, compared with 64,000 in November 1995.
However, latest Bureau of Statistics figures show the international holiday market is still growing overall, with increased visitors from emerging Asian markets as well as traditional markets.
There were about 376,000 short term overseas visitors to Australia last November, 9.5 per cent more than for the corresponding period a year earlier.
But the trend estimate for visitor arrivals dropped half a per cent last November for the fifth consecutive month.
HANSON WON'T BE INVITED TO LIBS FUNCTION AT LOGAN
The Liberal Party says Federal Independent, Pauline Hanson, will not be invited to a party function near Brisbane, though some members would like her there.
State Director, Jim Barron, says a decision to invite her to a meeting of the Logan Village branch was taken without authority.
He says the branch chairman and the Federal Electoral Council head have since pointed out to members that it's the Party's position not to invite Ms Hanson to Liberal functions.
ANTHRAX OUTBREAK
A fresh outbreak of anthrax has been confirmed in northern Victoria.
Tests confirm the disease killed six non-milking cows on a farm near Tatura in the Goulburn Valley.
The property has been quarantined, with other stock being vaccinated and moved to another paddock.
Nearby properties are also being monitored.
However the Natural Resources Department says there is no link between the latest outbreak and three previous cases in the area.
The Department says the disease has never been found in dairy products, although it is providing certificates to overseas firms worried about the outbreak.
KELTY TO STAND AGAIN
Secretary to the Australian Council of Trade Unions, Bill Kelty, wants to stay on for another six years in the job, after 15 years at the helm.
The offices of President, Secretary and the three assistant secretaries, will become vacant at the ACTU's Congress in Brisbane on September the first.
Mr Kelty's nomination for Secretary comes amid increasing pressure from the Federal Government.
Late yesterday, he announced his intention to stand at the Industrial Relations Commission hearing into a wage claim for transport workers.
He attacked the Minster, Peter Reith, accusing him of telling lies and creating expectations throughout negotiations. -- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
